newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks remain up in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks remain up in late trade.

text.p: Taiwan share prices were holding to sever-year high levels in late Monday trade, as local factors outweighed investor caution on the eve of Hong Kong's handover to Beijing, brokers said.
With 63 minutes left at 0257 GMT, the index was up 95.78 points or 1.06 percent at 9,120.26.
Turnover was a brisk T$101 billion.
"Investors are concerned whether the Hong Kong handover ceremony can go smoothly," said HSBC James Capel research manager Alex Chen.

"They are also watching whether China-related shares in the Hong Kong stock market can experience a further celebration rally after the July 1 handover." Hong Kong's market reopens on July 3 after a long handover holiday.
Brokers said Taiwan investors were watching the government's attitude toward the market after the central bank said it would inject funds later on Monday into the banking system.
"Sentiment is very bullish, but we all know the government does not like to see the market overheated," Chen said. "We'll have to see whether the government will take moves to dampen the market."
Transport, chemical and food shares took turns to lead the gains. Constructions and steels were also strong.
Electronics shares were off highs, but remained 0.60 percent higher.
